properties.headline: Flood Warning issued August 7 at 7:42AM CDT until August 7 at 11:45AM CDT by NWS Wichita KS
properties.description:
* WHAT...Flooding caused by excessive rainfall is expected.

* WHERE...Eastern Marion County in central Kansas...

* WHEN...Until 1145 AM CDT.

* IMPACTS...Flooding of rivers, creeks, streams, and other low-lying
and flood-prone locations is imminent or occurring. Low-water
crossings are inundated with water and may not be passable.

* ADDITIONAL DETAILS...
- At 742 AM CDT, emergency management reported heavy rain in the
warned area due to thunderstorms. Flooding is already occurring.
Between 2 and 5 inches of rain have fallen.
- Additional rainfall amounts up to 1 inch are possible in the
warned area.
- Some locations that will experience flooding include...
Marion, Florence, Burns, Lincolnville, Ramona, Lost Springs and
Pilsen.
- http://www.weather.gov/safety/flood
properties.instruction:
Turn around, don't drown when encountering flooded roads. Most flood
deaths occur in vehicles.

Be aware of your surroundings and do not drive on flooded roads.

properties.headline: Flood Warning issued August 6 at 8:04PM CDT until August 8 at 5:43AM CDT by NWS Corpus Christi TX
properties.description:
...The Flood Warning continues for the following rivers in Texas...

Nueces River Near Tilden affecting McMullen County.

For the Nueces River...including Cotulla, Tilden, Three Rivers,
Mathis, Bluntzer, Calallen...Minor flooding is forecast.

* WHAT...Minor flooding is occurring and minor flooding is forecast.

* WHERE...Nueces River near Tilden.

* WHEN...Until late Friday night.

* IMPACTS...At 16.0 feet, Moderate lowland flooding occurs. Hunting
cabins, oil field tanks and pumps are affected, and livestock
become isolated.

* ADDITIONAL DETAILS...
- At 7:30 PM CDT Thursday the stage was 16.0 feet.
- Bankfull stage is 11.0 feet.
- Forecast...The river is expected to fall below flood stage early
tomorrow afternoon and continue falling below action stage by
late tomorrow.
- Flood stage is 14.0 feet.
- http://www.weather.gov/safety/flood
properties.instruction:
Turn around, don't drown when encountering flooded roads. Most flood
deaths occur in vehicles.

Motorists should not attempt to drive around barricades or drive cars
through flooded areas.

Caution is urged when walking near riverbanks.

Even 6 inches of fast-moving flood water can knock you off your feet
and a depth of 2 feet will float your car. Never try to walk, swim,
or drive through such swift water. If you come upon flood waters,
stop, turn around and go another way.

Additional information is available at www.weather.gov/crp.

NWSheadline: FLOOD WARNING REMAINS IN EFFECT UNTIL LATE FRIDAY NIGHT

properties.headline: Flood Warning issued August 5 at 1:54PM AKDT until August 7 at 1:00PM AKDT by NWS Anchorage AK
properties.description:
* WHAT...Flooding caused by excessive rainfall continues.

* WHERE...Yentna River including Lake Creek.

* WHEN...Until 100 PM AKDT Friday.

* IMPACTS...Flooding of rivers, creeks, streams, and other low-lying
and flood-prone locations is imminent or occurring. Streams
continue to rise due to excess runoff from earlier rainfall.

* ADDITIONAL DETAILS...
- At 146 PM AKDT, river gauge reports indicate rises in water
levels from heavy rain across the warned area. Flooding is
ongoing. Between 1.5 and 3 inches of rain have fallen.
Additional rainfall amounts up to 0.25 inches are possible.
- For Yentna River at Lake Creek:
At 12:50pm the stage was 22.4 feet.
Flood Stage is 20.5 feet.
Forecast: A crest around 22.4 feet is expected around 4:00pm
Wednesday.
-The Yentna River at Lake Creek is forecast to go below flood
stage Saturday morning August 8th.

Impacts:
Between 21 and 22 feet, several lodges may have water in or
around low-lying cabins.




- Http://www.weather.gov/safety/flood
properties.instruction:
Stay tuned to further developments by listening to your local radio,
television, or NOAA Weather Radio for further information.

* WHEN...Until late Friday night.
